overview: Ireland is an island country in north-western Europe. It covers most of the island of Ireland; the north-east of the island is Northern Ireland, which is part of the United Kingdom. Its capital and largest city is Dublin. Ireland became independent from the United Kingdom in the 1920s and joined what is now the European Union in 1973. Irish and English are both official languages.

geography.text: Ireland is often called the Emerald Isle because of its green fields, kept lush by frequent rain from the Atlantic. The centre of the island is a low plain of farmland, lakes and peat bogs, ringed by coastal hills and mountains. The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and in the British Isles, and the rugged west coast includes the Cliffs of Moher.

history.text: Christianity reached Ireland in the 400s, and its monasteries became famous centres of learning. English, and later British, rule tightened from the 1100s onwards. The Great Famine of the 1840s killed about a million people and forced another million to emigrate. After the Easter Rising of 1916 and a war of independence, most of Ireland became independent in 1922.

events.title: Christianity arrives
events.text: Saint Patrick is traditionally credited with bringing Christianity to Ireland.

events.title: Anglo-Norman invasion
events.text: Anglo-Norman forces land in Ireland, beginning centuries of English rule.

events.title: Great Famine
events.text: Potato blight causes a famine that kills about a million people.

events.title: Easter Rising
events.text: Irish republicans rebel against British rule in Dublin.

events.title: Good Friday Agreement
events.text: A peace deal is agreed for Northern Ireland.

government.text: Ireland is a parliamentary republic. Voters elect the Dáil, the lower house of the Oireachtas (parliament), which chooses the Taoiseach, or Prime Minister. The President is elected directly every seven years. Ireland joined what is now the European Union in 1973 and is militarily neutral.

economy.text: Ireland has one of the highest incomes per person in the world on paper, partly because many large American technology and pharmaceutical companies have their European headquarters there for its low company tax. Farming, especially beef and dairy, food and tourism are also important.

culture.text: Ireland has produced four Nobel Prize winners in literature, including W. B. Yeats and Samuel Beckett, as well as James Joyce and Oscar Wilde. Irish traditional music and dance spread worldwide. Saint Patrick's Day, 17 March, is celebrated around the world.

items.title: Irish language
items.text: Irish (Gaeilge) is the first official language; English is the second.

items.title: Book of Kells
items.text: A richly decorated manuscript of the Gospels, made around 800.

items.title: Riverdance
items.text: The 1994 dance show that made Irish dancing famous worldwide.

sport.text: Ireland's own Gaelic games, hurling and Gaelic football, are its most watched sports, played by amateurs for their local county. Rugby union is also very strong, and the team plays as one side for the whole island. Horse racing is a national passion.

items.title: Hurling
items.text: One of the world's fastest field sports, more than 3,000 years old.

items.title: All-Ireland finals
items.text: Gaelic football and hurling finals fill Croke Park, holding 82,000 people.

items.title: Six Nations
items.text: Ireland won the rugby Grand Slam in 2009, 2018 and 2023.
